title: דברים פרק 24
english: When a man hath taken a wife, and married her, and it come to pass that she find no favour in his eyes, because he hath found some uncleanness in her: then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
And when she is departed out of his house, she may go and be another man's wife.
And if the latter husband hate her, and write her a bill of divorcement, and giveth it in her hand, and sendeth her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, which took her to be his wife;

Her former husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before the Lord: and thou shalt not cause the land to sin, which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance.
When a man hath taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business: but he shall be free at home one year, and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken.
No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge: for he taketh a man's life to pledge.
If a man be found stealing any of his brethren of the children of Israel, and maketh merchandise of him, or selleth him; then that thief shall die; and thou shalt put evil away from among you.
Take heed in the plague of leprosy, that thou observe diligently, and do according to all that the priests the Levites shall teach you: as I commanded them, so ye shall observe to do.
Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt.
When thou dost lend thy brother any thing, thou shalt not go into his house to fetch his pledge.
Thou shalt stand abroad, and the man to whom thou dost lend shall bring out the pledge abroad unto thee.
And if the man be poor, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge:
In any case thou shalt deliver him the pledge again when the sun goeth down, that he may sleep in his own raiment, and bless thee: and it shall be righteousness unto thee before the Lord thy God.
Thou shalt not oppress an hired servant that is poor and needy, whether he be of thy brethren, or of thy strangers that are in thy land within thy gates:
At his day thou shalt give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it; for he is poor, and setteth his heart upon it: lest he cry against thee unto the Lord, and it be sin unto thee.
The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.
Thou shalt not pervert the judgment of the stranger, nor of the fatherless; nor take a widow's raiment to pledge:
But thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee thence: therefore I command thee to do this thing.

When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hands.
When thou beatest thine olive tree, thou shalt not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
When thou gatherest the grapes of thy vineyard, thou shalt not glean it afterward: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt: therefore I command thee to do this thing.
ai_explanation: אדם יכול לגרש את אשתו אם היא אינה מוצאת חן בעיניו, משום שמצא בה דבר פגום או התנהגות בלתי מוסרית, גם אם אין בכך חיוב לגרשה. עליו לכתוב לה גט, למסור אותו לה ולשלחה מביתו.
האישה יוצאת מבית בעלה הראשון, הולכת ונישאת לאיש אחר.
אם גם הבעל השני אינו אוהב אותה, הוא יכול לכתוב לה גט, למסור אותו לה ולשלחה, או שהבעל השני מת.
יש להחזיר לעני את המשכון עם שקיעת השמש, כדי שיוכל לישון בבגדו. העני יברך את המחזיר, והחזרת המשכון תיחשב גם לצדקה לפני ה'.
אסור לנצל שכיר עני, ובכלל זה גר שאין לו נחלה משלו. השכיר תלוי במעסיקו, ולכן התורה מבקשת למנוע מהמעסיק לנצל את מצבו.
יש לשלם לשכיר את שכרו עד סוף יום עבודתו, לפני שקיעת השמש, מפני שהוא מצפה לשכר כדי לקנות את מזונו. אם לא ישולם בזמן, הוא עלול להתפלל נגד המעסיק, והדבר ייחשב לו לחטא גם אם נעשה בשגגה.
אין להעניש אבות בגלל חטאי בניהם, או בנים בגלל חטאי אבותיהם. כל אדם יומת רק בגלל חטאו שלו.
אין להטות את משפט הגר והיתום, משום שהם חסרי הגנה וקל לפגוע בהם; השופט נדרש לזהירות יתרה בעניינם. כמו כן, אסור לקחת בגד של אלמנה כמשכון, בשונה ממשכון של אנשים אחרים.
עליכם לזכור שהייתם עבדים במצרים ושה' הושיע אתכם משם. לכן עליכם לדאוג לזכויותיהם של אנשים סובלים אחרים, מתוך זיכרון ההתעללות שעברתם.
אם שכחת בשדה עומר, צרור שיבולים קשורות, אסור לך לחזור לקחת אותו; הוא יינתן לגר, ליתום ולאלמנה. אם תוותר על מה ששכחת לטובת החלשים, ה' יברך אותך במעשה ידיך.
בעת חבטת הזיתים אין לחפש ולאסוף את הזיתים שנשארו בין הענפים או שלא הבשילו לגמרי. גם שיירים אלה יינתנו לגר, ליתום ולאלמנה, אף שיש לך זכות עליהם.
לאחר בציר הכרם אין לאסוף את העוללות, כלומר את הענבים שלא נוצרו כאשכול. הם יינתנו לגר, ליתום ולאלמנה.
יש לזכור שהיית עבד במצרים ושאתה מכיר את מצבו של מי שאין לו דבר ואת שמחתו במציאות כאלה. מתוך מה שעבר עליך תוכל להבין ולקיים מצווה זו.
ai_explanation_en: A man who marries a woman and later finds her displeasing because he sees something flawed in her—or behavior he considers immoral, though not necessarily grounds requiring divorce—may decide to separate from her. He must write and give her a bill of divorce and send her away from his home.
After leaving her husband’s home, she may marry another man.
If her second husband also does not love her, he may write her a bill of divorce, give it to her, and send her away; alternatively, the second husband may die.

Even though she is free to marry someone else, she may not return to marry her first husband after marrying another. This permanent prohibition prevents sexual promiscuity and partner-swapping under a formally legal cover, so that the land is not led into sin.

A man who takes a new wife—either a woman who has never married or one who is new to him—must not serve in the army, risk his life in war, or be assigned any military work, including home-front duties. He is to be free from state obligations and devoted to his wife at home for one year, bringing her joy.
A creditor may not take either of the two millstones—the lower stone or the upper stone—as security for a debt. Taking the tools used to prepare bread is like taking away a person’s life.
Anyone who kidnaps an Israelite, exploits or enslaves him, abuses him, or otherwise mistreats him and then sells him must be put to death, thereby removing evil from the community.
The people must carefully observe all the laws concerning the affliction of leprosy and follow the instructions given by the Levitical priests, whom God commanded to teach these matters.

As an additional warning, they must remember what God did to Miriam, the prophetess and sister of Moses, during the journey from Egypt. She suffered leprosy and remained isolated for a week; although the people respectfully waited for her, her status did not exempt her from the disease and isolation.
When collecting a debt, a creditor may not enter the debtor’s house to take his pledge.

The creditor may demand a pledge worth the amount owed, but must remain outside and let the debtor bring it out. This respects the debtor’s dignity, since entering his home and choosing an item from his possessions would humiliate him.
If the debtor is poor and can offer only an outer garment that also serves as bedding or a blanket, the creditor may keep it as security but may not sleep while it is in his possession.

Return the pledge at sunset so the poor person can sleep in his own clothing. He will bless you for restoring what he needs, and beyond his blessing, this act will be counted as righteousness before the Lord your God.

Do not exploit a poor and needy hired worker, whether he is one of your people or a resident foreigner. Since hired workers generally lacked land and depended on their employers, the Torah seeks to prevent employers from taking advantage of this vulnerable position.

Pay the worker his wages on the day he works, before sunset, because he may depend on that daily payment to buy food. If you delay payment—even unintentionally—his resulting suffering may lead him to cry out to God against you, and you will be guilty.
Fathers must not be put to death for their children’s sins, nor children for their fathers’ sins. Each person is to be put to death only for his or her own sin, not for the wrongdoing of a relative.

Do not distort the judgment of a stranger or an orphan, because both lack protection and are especially vulnerable to harm. Likewise, do not take a widow’s garment as a pledge; unlike other people, the widow is specifically protected from having her clothing taken.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you. Because you experienced oppression, you must protect the rights of other suffering people.

If you forget a sheaf in your field, do not return to take it; leave it for the stranger, orphan, and widow. Since the forgetting was beyond your control, willingly relinquish the sheaf for the needy, and God will bless you for not insisting on reclaiming what you overlooked.

When beating your olive tree to remove its fruit, do not search through the branches afterward for olives that remained, whether hidden among the leaves or not fully ripened. Those remaining olives must be left for the stranger, orphan, and widow, requiring you to give up even small remnants to those in need.
After harvesting your vineyard, do not gather the individual grapes that did not form proper clusters. Leave them for the stranger, orphan, and widow.

Remember your desperate condition as a slave in Egypt and how meaningful even small provisions would have been to someone with nothing. Because of that experience, you can understand and fulfill this commandment to leave such produce for the needy.

did_you_know.text_en: The Torah calls the document a “sefer keritut,” while the Sages call it a “get.” The word “keritut” is connected with the idea of cutting off and ending the relationship.

did_you_know.text_en: The two millstones were a lower stone and an upper stone. Without either one, grain could not be ground, so taking one away threatened a family’s ability to obtain food.

did_you_know.text: הפסוק מדגיש שחטיפת אדם ומכירתו אינן גניבה רגילה של רכוש, אלא פגיעה חמורה בחירותו של אדם. בעולם העתיק, שבו עבדות הייתה נפוצה, התורה אוסרת במיוחד למכור בן־עם לעבד.

did_you_know.text_en: The verse stresses that kidnapping and selling a person is not ordinary theft, but a serious attack on human freedom. In the ancient world, where slavery was common, the Torah especially condemns selling a fellow Israelite into slavery.

did_you_know.text: „צרעת” המקראית אינה בהכרח מחלת הצרעת המוכרת כיום. זהו שם למצבי עור שונים שנבדקו בידי הכוהנים בעיקר כדי לקבוע את מעמדו הטקסי של האדם.

did_you_know.text_en: Biblical “tzaraat” is not necessarily the disease known today as leprosy. It refers to various skin conditions examined by priests, mainly to determine a person’s ritual status.

did_you_know.text: הבגד שנלקח כמשכון שימש לעיתים גם כשמיכה בלילה. לכן החזרתו לפני השינה היא לא רק כלל כלכלי, אלא הגנה על צרכיו הבסיסיים של העני.

did_you_know.text_en: A garment taken as security could also serve as a blanket at night. Returning it before bedtime was therefore not merely an economic rule, but protection of a poor person’s basic needs.

did_you_know.text: פועלים עניים בעולם הקדום חיו לעיתים משכרו של אותו יום, ולא מחסכונות חודשיים. עיכוב בתשלום עלול היה להשאיר את משפחתם בלי מזון.

did_you_know.text_en: Poor laborers in the ancient world often lived on that day’s wages rather than monthly savings. Delaying payment could leave their families without food.

did_you_know.text: בבציר אסור היה לעבור שוב ושוב על כל הגפן כדי לאסוף כל ענב. התורה דורשת להשאיר חלק מן היבול למי שאין להם שדה, וכך יוצרת דרך מכובדת לעזור להם.
did_you_know.text_he: בבציר אסור היה לעבור שוב ושוב על כל הגפן כדי לאסוף כל ענב. התורה דורשת להשאיר חלק מן היבול למי שאין להם שדה, וכך יוצרת דרך מכובדת לעזור להם.
did_you_know.text_en: During the grape harvest, a farmer was not to go over every vine repeatedly to collect every last grape. The Torah required leaving part of the crop for people without land, creating a dignified way to support them.
